title: The same canonical map at two independent input families
statement: Use the actual operations, expression objects, completion units, and isomorphism/basic/canonical-map generators of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. Given two families $M,K$ and $M',K'$ of system and integral inputs of the same schemes, define three synchronized relations. A synchronized isomorphism is one of the recorded pullback or direct-image compositors, open compositor, tensor associator, pull/tensor map, open base-change map, clopen comparison, compact-support expansion or open projection formula, evaluated at both families using the same geometric data. A synchronized basic map is the hom or inverse of such an isomorphism, or the recorded pull/open unit or counit, proper/open mate, exchange, projection, compactification exchange or compactification projection, again evaluated at both families using identical parameters. A synchronized canonical pair transports each integral basic map by that family's actual completion-unit inverse and completion unit, and closes these generators under identity, composition, and every unary or binary expression context. Composition retains the intermediate geometric/admissibility witnesses at both families. The four indices are the actual system and integral maps at the two families; there is no arbitrary-arrow constructor. Each projection is a pair in the existing canonical-map relation, and every existing canonical pair has its diagonal synchronized evaluation. This is a refinement of that existing relation, not a replacement for any operation or map.
